title: DARIS: An Oversubscribed Spatio-Temporal Scheduler for Real-Time DNN Inference on GPUs
problem: GPUs face underutilization in DNN inference workloads due to coarse-grained scheduling that cannot exploit fine-grained spatial and temporal concurrency.
motivation: Real-time DNN inference demands require meeting deadlines while maximizing GPU utilization in edge and inference-focused deployments.
method: DARIS uses priority-based real-time scheduling combining NVIDIA MPS (Multi-Process Service) for spatial sharing and CUDA streaming for temporal partitioning. Synchronization-based staging enables zero-delay DNN migration between GPU partitions. Oversubscription mechanism analyzes GPU concurrency.
key_novelty: Oversubscribed spatial-temporal scheduling for real-time DNNs combining MPS and CUDA streaming with zero-delay migration.
contributions: All high-priority tasks meet deadlines; low-priority miss rate under 2%
33% better high-priority response times vs low-priority tasks
limitations: Evaluation primarily on GPUs; generalization to other accelerators not discussed.
primary_theme: Oversubscribed spatio-temporal scheduling for real-time DNN inference
